posts.title: Adobe Stardust Explained: Design Agent Skills on EDS
posts.excerpt: What Adobe Stardust actually is: a skill in the public adobe/skills repo, not a product. It builds on impeccable, the 57K-star UX design skill library that does the actual design work. Walkthrough of the four steps (extract, direction, prototype, build into EDS), the human gate at prototypes, and three da.live blocks compared across a Google Stitch baseline and two Stardust runs.

posts.title: Top Models Compared: 4 Frontier Models, 1 Prompt
posts.excerpt: Four frontier models, GPT 5.6, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Claude Fable 5, each building the same portfolio site from the exact same 1,032-line prompt on 48 files of context. A tab-by-tab walkthrough of what each one built, pen-and-paper notebook grading, and an AI-picked winner, with the final site merged from the best pieces of all four.

posts.title: After a Year: Where I Think Knowledge Work Is Heading
posts.excerpt: The long-form companion to the Patterns of Work video. A year of building with AI almost every day, mapped as five layers, from one person amplified to where human and agentic managers share one context, with a spine of context, governance, observability, and evals running through all five and a shared-context foundation underneath. Includes the team-channel idea: tag an agent where the context already lives and it inherits the whole channel. Where I think knowledge work is heading, hedged where my conviction runs ahead of my receipts.

posts.title: Patterns of Work: Five Layers of Working with AI
posts.excerpt: An honest, unfiltered take on how we work with AI, mapped as five layers, from one person amplified up to where human and agentic managers share one common context. The real shift: it is not about data readiness, it is about getting agents to work alongside us on a shared surface, with real trust, security, observability, and governance underneath. A live hand-drawn talk, kept raw with minimal editing.

posts.title: Continuous Executive Agent V3.0: The Second Brain
posts.excerpt: Giving a 24/7 autonomous coding agent a real memory system, and why storage and retrieval are the hard part of agentic systems. A five-type memory taxonomy, automatic storage wired through lifecycle hooks, and agentic natural-language retrieval where the agent decides what past knowledge serves the goal in front of it. My first research-to-design-to-build cycle end to end. Open source.

posts.title: Theming a Brand-New EDS Site with Google Stitch + MCP
posts.excerpt: A 3-step approach to theming a greenfield EDS site: define what the theme could be, generate it in Google Stitch, then wire the design back into the site through the Stitch MCP server. Claude Opus 4.7 driving in a single ~20-minute prompt, traced in MLflow down to the tool calls, including the call-to-action miss and the lesson to theme the site and teaser as separate passes.
